objective: Derive a finite realizability-aware capped-cost closure criterion and certificate specification for universal k-edit tree leaf repair.

atomic_claims.text: Capped exact branch profiles have cardinality at most 6*(k+1)^5+60*(k+1)^59+240*(k+1)^239.
The least seed and transition closure consists exactly of the realizable capped profiles of old-star-colored pendant trees.
Universal k-edit tree repair is equivalent to the threshold passing every valid root tuple over reachable profiles.
A checked closed superset suffices for a positive certificate; a negative certificate needs reachable derivations and complete capped-vector checks.

assumptions: k is a fixed nonnegative integer; edit costs are nonnegative and charge old edges only.
The old pendant branches are finite simple subcubic trees with proper star six-edge-colorings.
C08's complete labeled signature and exact cost recurrence are used, without discarding labels or cyclic constraints.
risks: No closure computation or implementation was executed.
Coordinate-wise legal abstract profiles need not be realizable.
The finite upper bound may be far too large for practical exhaustive closure.
The theorem is a tree-only decision reduction and does not assert any universal sufficient edit budget.
A high-cost coloring alone is not a certificate that all lower-cost repairs fail.
